name: The Robinson household at Wolf Point
head: robinson_alexander

arrival.note: NOT DATED AND BOUNDED FROM ABOVE. 'It is not known just when Robinson settled in Chicago, but he had been here, at least two seasons, and with Antoine Ouilmette had cultivated the field belonging to the fort, raising thereon corn, when Captain Bradley arrived to rebuild Fort Dearborn in 1816.' Two seasons before 1816 would put him here by 1814; 1816 is the year the source actually fixes and is the conservative reading. THE SOURCE'S OWN WORDS ARE 'IT IS NOT KNOWN' and the grade says so. AN INDEPENDENT TABLE PRINTS THE YEAR THIS CARD'S OWN REASONING ALREADY IMPLIES, AND THE VALUE STILL DOES NOT MOVE. Moses and Kirkland, History of Chicago vol. 1 (1895), printed pages 78-79, the table headed LIST OF ACTUAL SETTLERS AT CHICAGO, PRIOR TO 1830 (data/research/books/records/moses_kirkland_v1_actual_settlers_pre_1830.json). It is an 1895 compilation crediting Hurlbut's Chicago Antiquities pp. 37-8 three lines above itself, every row transcription_mediated and none scan_verified, so NOTHING READ OFF IT IS GRADED ABOVE `inferred` HERE. Row bk_mose1_as_029 reads 'Robinson, Alex', YEAR 1814, remarks 'Paid taxes in 1825, voted in 1826 and 1830' — three civic acts at three dates, all three of which this card already holds, which is what makes the books crosswalk call it the strongest merge in its pass. 1814 IS EXACTLY TWO SEASONS BEFORE 1816, which is the interval Andreas's sentence gives and the interval this field was bounded from. THE VALUE IS LEFT AT 1816 ON PURPOSE: this field is a bound and says so, the table is an 1895 compilation at second hand, and replacing a stated upper bound with a tier-3 year would trade a defensible shape for a sharper number. The agreement is what is recorded. WHAT DOES NOT FOLLOW: the table's own preamble bounds it BEFORE 1830 and its remarks are civic acts of 1825-1830. A man on it is not thereby at Chicago on 1835-07-01, and this edit moves no residence, no `present_on_scene_date` and no grade. The identity is the books crosswalk's landed merge (T-0961) and is not re-opened here.

origin.value: Mackinaw; his father a Scots trader, his mother an Ottawa woman

THE SETTLERS TABLE'S NATIVITY CELL FOR HIM IS NOT A NATIVITY AND IS REFUSED AS WHAT IT IS. Row bk_mose1_as_029 prints 'Indian Chief' in the column where a birthplace belongs — an office set in a nativity cell. It says nothing about where he was born, it does not touch the Mackinaw this field carries from Andreas, and it is recorded here so that a later pass does not read the cell as a place.

reason_for_coming.value: The country trade at the forks
reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THIS HOUSEHOLD'S OWN RECORDED TRADE, WHICH IS NOT ITS MOTIVE. The head is recorded as trader, and this names the documented draw that trade answered in this town in this decade. It does not claim to know why these people came. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

lives_at.note: Wau-Bun, describing 1831: 'Near him [Wentworth's tavern] were two or three log cabins occupied by Robinson, the Pottowattamie chief, and some of his wife's connexions.' data/structures/robinson_caldwell_cabins.json exists on that single sentence and carries review_required: true for the same reason this household does. Andreas independently puts him at Wolf Point with a store or trading-house in the later part of his residence.

works_at.note: A trading house at Wolf Point is where his trade was carried on, and the cabins are the only Wolf Point building this dataset attaches to him. Whether the store was one of the cabins or a separate building is not stated.

present_on_scene_date.note: PRESENT ON 1 JULY 1835 ON THE BEST READING AND THE SOURCES DO NOT SAY SO IN TERMS. Andreas: 'After the Indians were removed beyond the Mississippi, he settled with his family on his reservation on the Desplaines' - i.e. he leaves Chicago AFTER the removal, and the removal is later than the scene date under either dating this project holds. The value is derived and not documented because no source places this household at Wolf Point on any date in 1835.

persons.name: Alexander Robinson (Che-che-pin-qua)

birth_year.note: Andreas gives 1762 'according to popular belief, and his age as stated at the time of his death, although the years of his life are somewhat doubtful' - the source's own hedge, carried rather than smoothed.

age_on_scene_date.note: Follows from a birth year the source itself calls doubtful.

occupation.note: 'During the latter part of his residence in Chicago, he lived at Wolf Point, where he had a store or trading-house' (Andreas). He was licensed to keep a tavern in Chicago on 8 June 1830, and the county clerk 'granted permits to sell goods to Alexander Robinson, John B. Beaubien, and Madore B. Beaubien' in 1831. He had earlier served as Indian interpreter under Dr Wolcott in 1825 and 1826 at $365 a year, and he is a chief of the united Potawatomi, Chippewa and Ottawa band - the office is not an occupation and is recorded in the person note.

appearance_bounds.source_title: Fifth census of the United States, 1830 — the division headed 'Peoria & Putnam Counties & Territory attached'
appearance_bounds.identity_rule: Surname and given name both agree between the 1830 reading 'Alexander Robinson' and the town person 'Alexander Robinson (Che-che-pin-qua)' in household hh_robinson_alexander. The 1830 line is carried as EARLIER EVIDENCE for that person and grades nothing on its own.
appearance_bounds.note: A BOUND ON PRESENCE IN A DISTRICT, AND NOT AT CHICAGO. The division is headed 'Peoria & Putnam Counties & Territory attached' and the schedule never writes the word Chicago — the Fox River and Du Page settlements are inside it — so this row bounds presence in that district in the summer of 1830 and puts no body in the town, which is why `here_by` is null. The record's own note says it first: 'Presence in that district in the summer of 1830; not a Chicago residence, and never an 1835 one'. Under the evidence ladder ratified 2026-09-03 a source EARLIER than the scene date corroborates and dates and never promotes, and a source LATER than it does not promote either. THE IDENTITY IS INFERRED AND THE PAGE IS NOT: the leaf is read scan_verified off the federal schedule, and what no source states is that the head of family on it is the person on this card. data/research/census_1830/resident_crosswalk.json joins them on a name agreement and says in terms that it grades nothing on its own. No grade moves here and the identity is neither reopened nor hardened.

persons.note: A CHIEF, A LICENSED TRADER AND A RECORDED VOTER OF THE SETTLEMENT. Andreas: born at Mackinaw about 1762, his father a Scots trader who had been an officer in the British army and his mother an Ottawa woman; he sheltered the Kinzie family after the 1812 massacre and carried Captain and Mrs Heald three hundred miles by bark canoe to Mackinaw. His personal property was assessed at $200 by the Peoria County assessor in 1825 and he is recorded as a voter in 1825, 1826 and 1830. He married Catherine Chevalier, daughter of the chief Francois Chevalier, on 28 September 1826, John Kinzie officiating as justice of the peace, and became chief of her father's band at his death. By the treaty of Prairie du Chien of July 1829 he was granted two sections on the Des Plaines; by Camp Tippecanoe in 1832 a life annuity of $200; and by the Chicago treaty of September 1833 a further $300 a year for life.

Andreas: married 28 September 1826 by John Kinzie, J.P.; daughter of Francois and Mary Ann Chevalier, her father chief of a united band of Potawatomi, Ottawa and Chippewa with his village at the Calumet; she died 7 August 1860 and is buried with her husband on the bank of the Des Plaines.

'John Robinson' at printed page 207 line 20 (33SQ-GYYJ-93G) is NOT 'Catherine Chevalier Robinson': The surname 'robinson' is carried by 1 person(s) of 1835 (Catherine Chevalier Robinson) and none of their given names is 'john'. The 1840 census heads 'James Robinson' and 'John Robinson' are both refused against her in the repository on a given-name conflict; she is the only Robinson woman the 1835 layer holds.

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('robinson_catherine:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

research_note: A DOCUMENTED HOUSEHOLD OF THREE NAMED OR COUNTED PEOPLE WHO WERE LIVING AT WOLF POINT WHEN THE TOWN GREW UP AROUND THEM. STANDING CONSTRAINT. AGENTS.md: the final removal of the Potawatomi from Chicago occurred in August 1835, inside this project's first target year and six weeks AFTER the scene date; Native presence, representation and depiction are not research gaps to be filled by inference, and v1 ships no human figures at all. This record is a dataset entry that states what named sources say about a named person and adds nothing. It carries review_required so that no scene containing it can be marked released before the consultation the project has committed to. TWO DATING PROBLEMS ARE RECORDED AND NOT RESOLVED. First, Andreas dates the last great assembly and the departure for the Missouri to 1836 under Captain Russell and Billy Caldwell, while this project's own source chicagology_lastwardance places the last war dance at Chicago on 18 August 1835; the two readings differ by a year and both are AFTER 1 July 1835, so the scene date is unaffected and the disagreement is recorded rather than averaged. Second, Wau-Bun describes 1831 and this scene is 1835; the structure record already says its four-year run is 'the longest unsupported run in this dataset' and that the years it crosses are the years of the removal. This household claims that the people were there, on the same evidence and with the same warning.
